stimuli.title: Eight persons — Isha, Jatin, Gauri, Charu, Kavya, Deepak, Uday, and Sneha — live in an eight-flat four-storey building. The bottom floor is 1 and the top floor is 4. Each floor has two flats: Flat A and Flat B. Flat A is to the west of Flat B.
stimuli.body:
Study the following information carefully and answer the questions that follow:
• Charu lives on the bottommost floor.
• Gauri lives immediately to the west of Kavya.
• There is exactly one floor between the floors of Jatin and Sneha, and both live in Flat B.
• The number of floors above Charu is equal to the number of floors below Gauri.
• Uday lives immediately above Charu in the same flat.
• Uday lives immediately to the west of Isha.
• Deepak lives on Floor 3 in Flat A.

(Note: Flat A is immediately to the west of Flat B on each floor).
stimuli.solution: Floor 4: Flat A = Gauri, Flat B = Kavya | Floor 3: Flat A = Deepak, Flat B = Jatin | Floor 2: Flat A = Uday, Flat B = Isha | Floor 1: Flat A = Charu, Flat B = Sneha

• Jatin sits second to the right of Bhavna.
• Bhavna sits immediately to the left of Wami.
• Bharat faces the outside.
• Chitra sits diametrically opposite to Wami.
• Aarav sits immediately to the left of Jatin.
• Zara sits second to the right of Jatin.
• Chitra sits third to the left of Esha.

(Note: Positions are numbered 1 to 8 consecutively in a clockwise direction).
stimuli.solution: Seat 1: Esha (facing Center), Seat 2: Bharat (facing Outside), Seat 3: Zara (facing Center), Seat 4: Chitra (facing Outside), Seat 5: Jatin (facing Center), Seat 6: Aarav (facing Outside), Seat 7: Bhavna (facing Center), Seat 8: Wami (facing Outside)

stimuli.title: Eight persons — Deepak, Geeta, Farhan, Rohan, Isha, Uday, Tanvi, and Yogesh — have their preliminary examinations scheduled on two different dates (7th and 21st) across four months (March, April, May, and June).
stimuli.body:
Study the following information carefully and answer the questions that follow:
• The number of persons attending the exam before Geeta is equal to the number of persons attending after Yogesh.
• Rohan attends the exam in June.
• Only two persons attends the exam between Isha and Tanvi.
• Yogesh attends the exam immediately after Deepak.
• Only two persons attends the exam between Geeta and Yogesh.
• Only two persons attends the exam between Deepak and Uday.
• Only one person attends the exam between Rohan and Uday.
• Only one person attends the exam between Geeta and Tanvi.
• Farhan attends the exam on 21st June.

(Note: The order of months is March, April, May, and June. Each month has exams on the 7th and 21st).
stimuli.solution: March 7th: Isha; March 21th: Deepak; April 7th: Yogesh; April 21th: Tanvi; May 7th: Uday; May 21th: Geeta; June 7th: Rohan; June 21th: Farhan

stimuli.title: Caselet: Student enrollment in competitive exam streams
stimuli.body:
Read the passage carefully to answer the following questions:
In an institute of 600 aspirants, students opted for coaching across three exam streams: Banking, SSC, and Railways.
• 120 students opted ONLY for Banking.
• 150 students opted ONLY for SSC.
• 100 students opted ONLY for Railways.
• 50 students opted for BOTH Banking and SSC, but not Railways.
• 40 students opted for BOTH SSC and Railways, but not Banking.
• 60 students opted for BOTH Banking and Railways, but not SSC.
• 30 students opted for ALL THREE exam streams.
The remaining students did not opt for any of these three streams.
stimuli.solution: Total: 600 | Banking: 260 | SSC: 270 | Railways: 230 | None: 50

questions.stem:
In the question below, statements are given followed by two conclusions. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the given statements.

Statements:
• Only a few laptops are tablets.
• All tablets are computers.
• No computers is a mobiles.

Conclusions:
I. Some laptops are not tablets.
II. No tablets is a mobiles.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation:
1. 'Only a few laptops are tablets' implies both 'Some laptops are tablets' and 'Some laptops are NOT tablets'. Thus, Conclusion I definitely follows.
2. Since all tablets are inside computers and no computers is a mobiles, there is no intersection between tablets and mobiles. Hence, Conclusion II follows.

questions.stem:
In the question below, statements are given followed by two conclusions. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the given statements.

Statements:
• Only a few laptops are tablets.
• Few tablets are computers.
• All computers are mobiles.

Conclusions:
I. All laptops being tablets is a possibility.
II. Some tablets are mobiles.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation:
1. 'Only a few laptops are tablets' strictly forbids all laptops from being tablets. Hence, Conclusion I is NOT a valid possibility.
2. Since some tablets are computers and all computers are mobiles, the common portion of tablets and computers must also be mobiles. Hence, Conclusion II definitely follows.

questions.stem:
In these questions, relationships between different elements are shown in the statements. The statements are followed by two conclusions. Read the statements and select the correct option:

Statements: P > Q ≥ R = S; T ≤ U < R; W ≥ P

Conclusions: I. W > S    II. P > T
options: Either conclusion I or II is true
Both conclusions I and II are true
questions.explanation:
From the statements:
• W ≥ P > Q ≥ R = S ⇒ W > S (Conclusion I is definitely true).
• P > R and R > U ≥ T ⇒ P > T (Conclusion II is definitely true).
Both conclusions I and II are true.

questions.stem:
In these questions, relationships between different elements are shown in the statements. The statements are followed by two conclusions. Read the statements and select the correct option:

Statements: A ≥ B > C = D; E < F ≤ C; G > B

Conclusions: I. G > E    II. A ≥ F
options: Either conclusion I or II is true
Both conclusions I and II are true
questions.explanation:
From the statements:
• G > B > C ≥ F > E ⇒ G > E (Conclusion I is true).
• A ≥ B > C ≥ F ⇒ A > F, so A ≥ F is not definitely true. (Conclusion II is false).

questions.stem:
In these questions, relationships between different elements are shown in the statements. The statements are followed by two conclusions. Read the statements and select the correct option:

Statements: K ≤ L < M = N; O ≥ P > L; Q ≤ K

Conclusions: I. O > K    II. N > Q
options: Either conclusion I or II is true
Both conclusions I and II are true
questions.explanation:
From the statements:
• O ≥ P > L > K ⇒ O > K (Conclusion I is true).
• N = M > L > K ≥ Q ⇒ N > Q (Conclusion II is true).
Both conclusions are true.

questions.stem:
In these questions, relationships between different elements are shown in the statements. The statements are followed by two conclusions. Read the statements and select the correct option:

Statements: H > I < J ≤ K; L ≤ M < I; N ≥ K

Conclusions: I. H > M    II. L > N
options: Both conclusions I and II are true
Either conclusion I or II is true
questions.explanation:
From the statements:
• H > I and M > I: signs between H and M oppose. (Conclusion I cannot be definitely established).
• L ≤ M < I < J ≤ K ≤ N: L < N, not L > N. (Conclusion II is false).
Therefore, neither conclusion is true.

questions.stem:
In these questions, relationships between different elements are shown in the statements. The statements are followed by two conclusions. Read the statements and select the correct option:

Statements: V ≥ W > X = Y; Z ≤ Y; U < V

Conclusions: I. W < Z    II. V > X
options: Both conclusions I and II are true
Either conclusion I or II is true
questions.explanation:
From the statements:
• W > X = Y ≥ Z ⇒ W > Z (so W < Z is false).
• V ≥ W > X ⇒ V > X (Conclusion II is definitely true).

questions.stem:
Study the information carefully to answer the questions:
A family consists of seven members: P, Q, R, S, T, U, and V spanning three generations. There are two married couples.
• P is the paternal grandfather of V.
• Q is the only son of P.
• R is the daughter-in-law of P and mother of V.
• S is the sister of Q.
• T is the sister-in-law of R and is unmarried.
• U is the husband of S and father of a daughter.

How is Q related to V?
questions.explanation: P is the grandfather of V, and Q is the only son of P. R is the mother of V and wife of Q. Therefore, Q is the father of V.

questions.stem: How is S related to V?
questions.explanation: S is the sister of Q (V's father). Therefore, S is V's father's sister, which is Paternal Aunt.

questions.stem: How is U related to Q?
questions.explanation: U is the husband of S, who is Q's sister. Therefore, U is Q's sister's husband (Brother-in-law).

questions.stem: A person starts walking from Point A, walks 12 meters towards North to reach Point B. He then turns right (East) and walks 9 meters to reach Point C. He then turns right (South) and walks 12 meters to reach Point D. In which direction and at what shortest distance is Point D from Point A?
questions.explanation: Net North-South displacement = 12m North − 12m South = 0m. Net East displacement = 9m East. Hence, Point D is exactly 9 meters East of Point A.

questions.stem: How many such pairs of letters are there in the word 'COMPUTE', each of which has as many letters between them in the word (in both forward and backward directions) as they have between them in the English alphabetical series?

Female in B = 160, Female in D = 180. Total females (B+D) = 340.

questions.stem: The number of male employees in Branch B is what percent more or less than the number of female employees in Branch E?
questions.explanation:
Male in B = 200, Female in E = 180.
Difference = 200 − 180 = 20.
Percentage = (20 / 180) × 100% = 11.1% (more).

questions.stem: What is the average number of female employees working across all the five branches?
questions.explanation:

Average = 760 ÷ 5 = 152.

questions.stem: Find the difference between the total number of male employees in Branches C, D, and E together and the total number of female employees in Branches A, B, and C together.
questions.explanation:
Total males (C+D+E) = 300 + 120 + 240 = 660.
Total females (A+B+C) = 60 + 160 + 180 = 400.
Difference = 660 − 400 = 260.

questions.stem: If in another Branch F, the total number of employees is 25% more than that in Branch A, and the ratio of Male to Female employees in Branch F is 3 : 2, find the number of male employees in Branch F.
questions.explanation:
Total in Branch A = 240.
Total in Branch F = 240 × 1.25 = 300.
Male in Branch F = (3 / 5) × 300 = 180.

questions.stem: If each sold unit earns ₹1,500 and each unsold unit incurs a storage penalty of ₹200, what is the net earnings of the company in January?

In the following question, two equations I and II are given. You have to solve both equations and select the appropriate relation:

Equation I: x² − 15x + 56 = 0
Equation II: y² − 9y + 20 = 0
options: x = y or the relationship cannot be established
questions.explanation:
For Eq I: x² − 15x + 56 = 0 ⇒ (x − 7)(x − 8) = 0 ⇒ x = 7, 8.
For Eq II: y² − 9y + 20 = 0 ⇒ (y − 4)(y − 5) = 0 ⇒ y = 4, 5.
Comparing roots:
• 7 > 4 and 7 > 5
• 8 > 4 and 8 > 5
Hence, x > y.

questions.stem:
In the following question, two equations I and II are given. You have to solve both equations and select the appropriate relation:

Equation I: x² − 5x + 6 = 0
Equation II: y² − 13y + 42 = 0
options: x = y or the relationship cannot be established
questions.explanation:
For Eq I: x² − 5x + 6 = 0 ⇒ (x − 2)(x − 3) = 0 ⇒ x = 2, 3.
For Eq II: y² − 13y + 42 = 0 ⇒ (y − 6)(y − 7) = 0 ⇒ y = 6, 7.
Comparing roots:
• 2 < 6 and 2 < 7
• 3 < 6 and 3 < 7
Hence, x < y.

Equation II: y² − 7y + 12 = 0
options: x = y or the relationship cannot be established
questions.explanation:

Comparing roots:

• When x = −2: −2 < 3 and −2 < 4 (x < y)
Since opposite relationships hold, relationship cannot be established.

questions.stem:
What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following number series?
12, 7, 9, 16.5, 37, ?

What will come in place of (?) in the following number series?
15, 16, 24, 51, 115, ?
questions.explanation:
The difference between consecutive terms is cubes of consecutive integers:
• 16 − 15 = 1 (1³)
• 24 − 16 = 8 (2³)
• 51 − 24 = 27 (3³)
• 115 − 51 = 64 (4³)
• Next term = 115 + 5³ = 115 + 125 = 240.

questions.stem: A shopkeeper marks an article 40% above its cost price and sells it after allowing a discount of 15% on the marked price. If he earns a profit of ₹380, what was the cost price of the article?
questions.explanation:
Let Cost Price (CP) = 100x.
Marked Price (MP) = 100x × 1.40 = 140x.
Selling Price (SP) = 140x × (1 − 0.15) = 140x × 0.85 = 119x.
Profit = SP − CP = 119x − 100x = 19x.
Given: 19x = 380 ⇒ x = 20.
Cost Price = 100x = ₹2,000.

questions.stem: The difference between compound interest (compounded annually) and simple interest on a certain principal sum at 10% per annum for 2 years is ₹180. Find the principal sum.
questions.explanation:
For 2 years, the difference between CI and SI is given by:
Difference = P × (R / 100)²
180 = P × (10 / 100)² = P × (1 / 100)
P = 180 × 100 = ₹18,000.

questions.stem: A is 20% more efficient than B. B alone can complete a piece of work in 30 days. Both work together for 6 days, and then B leaves. In how many more days will A alone complete the remaining work?
questions.explanation:
Efficiency ratio of A : B = 120 : 100 = 6 : 5.
Total work = Efficiency of B × Days = 5 × 30 = 150 units.
Combined work done in 6 days = (6 + 5) × 6 = 66 units.
Remaining work = 150 − 66 = 84 units.
Time taken by A alone = 84 ÷ 6 = 14 days.

questions.stem: A vessel contains 80 litres of a mixture of milk and water in the ratio 3 : 1. If 16 litres of this mixture is taken out and replaced with 16 litres of pure water, what is the new ratio of milk to water in the vessel?
questions.explanation:
Initial volume = 80 L (Ratio 3 : 1):
• Milk = (3/4) × 80 = 60 L
• Water = (1/4) × 80 = 20 L
16 L removed:
• Milk removed = (3/4) × 16 = 12 L ⇒ Remaining Milk = 60 − 12 = 48 L
• Water removed = (1/4) × 16 = 4 L ⇒ Remaining Water = 20 − 4 = 16 L
16 L pure water added:
• New Water = 16 + 16 = 32 L
New Ratio of Milk : Water = 48 : 32 = 3 : 2.

questions.stem: Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 hours and Pipe B can fill it in 15 hours. A third pipe C can empty the full tank in 20 hours. If all three pipes are opened simultaneously, in how many hours will the empty tank be completely filled?
questions.explanation:
LCM of 12, 15, and 20 = 60 units (Total tank capacity).
• Efficiency of A = +60/12 = +5 units/h
• Efficiency of B = +60/15 = +4 units/h
• Efficiency of C = −60/20 = −3 units/h
Combined efficiency = 5 + 4 − 3 = 6 units/h.
Time to fill = 60 ÷ 6 = 10 hours.

questions.stem: The speed of a boat in still water is 18 km/h and the speed of the stream is 6 km/h. If the boat takes 4 hours more to travel a certain distance upstream than downstream, find the distance.
questions.explanation:
Downstream speed = 18 + 6 = 24 km/h.
Upstream speed = 18 − 6 = 12 km/h.
Let distance be D km.
Time upstream − Time downstream = 4 hours
(D / 12) − (D / 24) = 4 ⇒ D / 24 = 4 ⇒ D = 96 km.

questions.stem: Six years ago, the ratio of the ages of Kunal and Sagar was 6 : 5. Four years hence, the ratio of their ages will be 11 : 10. What is Sagar's present age?
questions.explanation:
Let ages 6 years ago be 6x and 5x.
Present ages = (6x + 6) and (5x + 6).
4 years hence, their ages will be (6x + 10) and (5x + 10).
Given: (6x + 10) / (5x + 10) = 11 / 10
60x + 100 = 55x + 110 ⇒ 5x = 10 ⇒ x = 2.
Sagar's present age = 5x + 6 = 5(2) + 6 = 16 years.

questions.stem: A and B entered into a partnership with initial investments of ₹15,000 and ₹20,000 respectively. After 4 months, A invested an additional ₹5,000, while B withdrew ₹5,000. If the total annual profit was ₹21,000, find A's share of the profit.
A train 240 meters long moving at a speed of 72 km/h crosses a railway platform in 25 seconds. What is the length of the platform?
questions.explanation:
Speed of train in m/s = 72 × (5/18) = 20 m/s.
Total distance covered in 25 seconds = Speed × Time = 20 × 25 = 500 meters.
Total distance = Length of train + Length of platform
500 = 240 + Platform Length
Platform Length = 500 − 240 = 260 meters.

questions.stem: The length and breadth of a rectangular field are in the ratio 5 : 2, and its perimeter is 98 meters. A circular lawn has a radius equal to the breadth of this rectangular field. Find the area of the circular lawn (taking π = 22/7).
questions.explanation:
Perimeter of rectangle = 2(l + b) = 98 ⇒ l + b = 49 m.
Ratio 5 : 2 ⇒ 7x = 49 ⇒ x = 7.
Length = 5 × 7 = 35 m, Breadth = 2 × 7 = 14 m.
Radius of circular lawn r = Breadth = 14 m.
Area of circular lawn = π × r² = (22/7) × 14 × 14 = 616 m².

Statements:
• Only a few banks are offices.
• All offices are cabins.
• No cabins is a rooms.

Conclusions:
I. Some banks are not offices.
II. No offices is a rooms.
options: Either conclusion I or II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation:

2. Since all offices are inside cabins and no cabins is a rooms, there is no intersection between offices and rooms. Hence, Conclusion II follows.

In the following question, two equations I and II are given. You have to solve both equations and select the appropriate relation:

questions.stem: A shopkeeper marks an article 40% above its cost price and sells it after allowing a discount of 15% on the marked price. If he earns a profit of ₹380, what was the cost price of the article?
questions.explanation:
Let Cost Price (CP) = 100x.
Marked Price (MP) = 100x × 1.40 = 140x.
Selling Price (SP) = 140x × (1 − 0.15) = 140x × 0.85 = 119x.
Profit = SP − CP = 119x − 100x = 19x.
Given: 19x = 380 ⇒ x = 20.
Cost Price = 100x = ₹2,000.

questions.stem: The difference between compound interest (compounded annually) and simple interest on a certain principal sum at 10% per annum for 2 years is ₹180. Find the principal sum.
questions.explanation:
For 2 years, the difference between CI and SI is given by:
Difference = P × (R / 100)²
180 = P × (10 / 100)² = P × (1 / 100)
P = 180 × 100 = ₹18,000.

questions.stem: A is 20% more efficient than B. B alone can complete a piece of work in 30 days. Both work together for 6 days, and then B leaves. In how many more days will A alone complete the remaining work?
questions.explanation:
Efficiency ratio of A : B = 120 : 100 = 6 : 5.
Total work = Efficiency of B × Days = 5 × 30 = 150 units.
Combined work done in 6 days = (6 + 5) × 6 = 66 units.
Remaining work = 150 − 66 = 84 units.
Time taken by A alone = 84 ÷ 6 = 14 days.

questions.stem: A vessel contains 80 litres of a mixture of milk and water in the ratio 3 : 1. If 16 litres of this mixture is taken out and replaced with 16 litres of pure water, what is the new ratio of milk to water in the vessel?
questions.explanation:
Initial volume = 80 L (Ratio 3 : 1):
• Milk = (3/4) × 80 = 60 L
• Water = (1/4) × 80 = 20 L
16 L removed:
• Milk removed = (3/4) × 16 = 12 L ⇒ Remaining Milk = 60 − 12 = 48 L
• Water removed = (1/4) × 16 = 4 L ⇒ Remaining Water = 20 − 4 = 16 L
16 L pure water added:
• New Water = 16 + 16 = 32 L
New Ratio of Milk : Water = 48 : 32 = 3 : 2.

questions.stem: Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 hours and Pipe B can fill it in 15 hours. A third pipe C can empty the full tank in 20 hours. If all three pipes are opened simultaneously, in how many hours will the empty tank be completely filled?
questions.explanation:
LCM of 12, 15, and 20 = 60 units (Total tank capacity).
• Efficiency of A = +60/12 = +5 units/h
• Efficiency of B = +60/15 = +4 units/h
• Efficiency of C = −60/20 = −3 units/h
Combined efficiency = 5 + 4 − 3 = 6 units/h.
Time to fill = 60 ÷ 6 = 10 hours.

questions.stem: The speed of a boat in still water is 18 km/h and the speed of the stream is 6 km/h. If the boat takes 4 hours more to travel a certain distance upstream than downstream, find the distance.
questions.explanation:
Downstream speed = 18 + 6 = 24 km/h.
Upstream speed = 18 − 6 = 12 km/h.
Let distance be D km.
Time upstream − Time downstream = 4 hours
(D / 12) − (D / 24) = 4 ⇒ D / 24 = 4 ⇒ D = 96 km.

questions.stem: Six years ago, the ratio of the ages of Kunal and Sagar was 6 : 5. Four years hence, the ratio of their ages will be 11 : 10. What is Sagar's present age?
questions.explanation:
Let ages 6 years ago be 6x and 5x.
Present ages = (6x + 6) and (5x + 6).
4 years hence, their ages will be (6x + 10) and (5x + 10).
Given: (6x + 10) / (5x + 10) = 11 / 10
60x + 100 = 55x + 110 ⇒ 5x = 10 ⇒ x = 2.
Sagar's present age = 5x + 6 = 5(2) + 6 = 16 years.

questions.stem: A and B entered into a partnership with initial investments of ₹15,000 and ₹20,000 respectively. After 4 months, A invested an additional ₹5,000, while B withdrew ₹5,000. If the total annual profit was ₹21,000, find A's share of the profit.
A train 240 meters long moving at a speed of 72 km/h crosses a railway platform in 25 seconds. What is the length of the platform?
questions.explanation:
Speed of train in m/s = 72 × (5/18) = 20 m/s.
Total distance covered in 25 seconds = Speed × Time = 20 × 25 = 500 meters.
Total distance = Length of train + Length of platform
500 = 240 + Platform Length
Platform Length = 500 − 240 = 260 meters.

questions.stem: The length and breadth of a rectangular field are in the ratio 5 : 2, and its perimeter is 98 meters. A circular lawn has a radius equal to the breadth of this rectangular field. Find the area of the circular lawn (taking π = 22/7).
questions.explanation:
Perimeter of rectangle = 2(l + b) = 98 ⇒ l + b = 49 m.
Ratio 5 : 2 ⇒ 7x = 49 ⇒ x = 7.
Length = 5 × 7 = 35 m, Breadth = 2 × 7 = 14 m.
Radius of circular lawn r = Breadth = 14 m.
Area of circular lawn = π × r² = (22/7) × 14 × 14 = 616 m².

questions.stem:
In the question below, statements are given followed by two conclusions. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the given statements.

Statements:
• Only a few circles are squares.
• All squares are triangles.
• No triangles is a rectangles.

Conclusions:
I. Some circles are not squares.
II. No squares is a rectangles.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation:
1. 'Only a few circles are squares' implies both 'Some circles are squares' and 'Some circles are NOT squares'. Thus, Conclusion I definitely follows.
2. Since all squares are inside triangles and no triangles is a rectangles, there is no intersection between squares and rectangles. Hence, Conclusion II follows.

questions.stem:

Statements:

• All triangles are rectangles.

II. Some squares are rectangles.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation:
1. 'Only a few circles are squares' strictly forbids all circles from being squares. Hence, Conclusion I is NOT a valid possibility.
2. Since some squares are triangles and all triangles are rectangles, the common portion of squares and triangles must also be rectangles. Hence, Conclusion II definitely follows.

options: Both conclusions I and II are true

questions.explanation:
From the statements:
• W ≥ P > Q ≥ R = S ⇒ W > S (Conclusion I is definitely true).
• P > R and R > U ≥ T ⇒ P > T (Conclusion II is definitely true).
Both conclusions I and II are true.

• A ≥ B > C ≥ F ⇒ A > F, so A ≥ F is not definitely true. (Conclusion II is false).

questions.stem:

questions.stem: A person starts walking from Point A, walks 12 meters towards North to reach Point B. He then turns right (East) and walks 9 meters to reach Point C. In the following question, two equations I and II are given. You have to solve both equations and select the appropriate relation:

Equation I: x² − 15x + 56 = 0
Equation II: y² − 9y + 20 = 0
options: x = y or the relationship cannot be established
questions.explanation:
For Eq I: x² − 15x + 56 = 0 ⇒ (x − 7)(x − 8) = 0 ⇒ x = 7, 8.
For Eq II: y² − 9y + 20 = 0 ⇒ (y − 4)(y − 5) = 0 ⇒ y = 4, 5.
Comparing roots:
• 7 > 4 and 7 > 5
• 8 > 4 and 8 > 5
Hence, x > y.

questions.stem: A shopkeeper marks an article 40% above its cost price and sells it after allowing a discount of 15% on the marked price. If he earns a profit of ₹380, what was the cost price of the article?
questions.explanation:
Let Cost Price (CP) = 100x.
Marked Price (MP) = 100x × 1.40 = 140x.
Selling Price (SP) = 140x × (1 − 0.15) = 140x × 0.85 = 119x.
Profit = SP − CP = 119x − 100x = 19x.
Given: 19x = 380 ⇒ x = 20.
Cost Price = 100x = ₹2,000.

questions.stem: The difference between compound interest (compounded annually) and simple interest on a certain principal sum at 10% per annum for 2 years is ₹180. Find the principal sum.
questions.explanation:
For 2 years, the difference between CI and SI is given by:
Difference = P × (R / 100)²
180 = P × (10 / 100)² = P × (1 / 100)
P = 180 × 100 = ₹18,000.

questions.stem: A is 20% more efficient than B. B alone can complete a piece of work in 30 days. Both work together for 6 days, and then B leaves. In how many more days will A alone complete the remaining work?
questions.explanation:
Efficiency ratio of A : B = 120 : 100 = 6 : 5.
Total work = Efficiency of B × Days = 5 × 30 = 150 units.
Combined work done in 6 days = (6 + 5) × 6 = 66 units.
Remaining work = 150 − 66 = 84 units.
Time taken by A alone = 84 ÷ 6 = 14 days.

questions.stem: A vessel contains 80 litres of a mixture of milk and water in the ratio 3 : 1. If 16 litres of this mixture is taken out and replaced with 16 litres of pure water, what is the new ratio of milk to water in the vessel?
questions.explanation:
Initial volume = 80 L (Ratio 3 : 1):
• Milk = (3/4) × 80 = 60 L
• Water = (1/4) × 80 = 20 L
16 L removed:
• Milk removed = (3/4) × 16 = 12 L ⇒ Remaining Milk = 60 − 12 = 48 L
• Water removed = (1/4) × 16 = 4 L ⇒ Remaining Water = 20 − 4 = 16 L
16 L pure water added:
• New Water = 16 + 16 = 32 L
New Ratio of Milk : Water = 48 : 32 = 3 : 2.

questions.stem: Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 hours and Pipe B can fill it in 15 hours. A third pipe C can empty the full tank in 20 hours. If all three pipes are opened simultaneously, in how many hours will the empty tank be completely filled?
questions.explanation:
LCM of 12, 15, and 20 = 60 units (Total tank capacity).
• Efficiency of A = +60/12 = +5 units/h
• Efficiency of B = +60/15 = +4 units/h
• Efficiency of C = −60/20 = −3 units/h
Combined efficiency = 5 + 4 − 3 = 6 units/h.
Time to fill = 60 ÷ 6 = 10 hours.

questions.stem: The speed of a boat in still water is 18 km/h and the speed of the stream is 6 km/h. If the boat takes 4 hours more to travel a certain distance upstream than downstream, find the distance.
questions.explanation:
Downstream speed = 18 + 6 = 24 km/h.
Upstream speed = 18 − 6 = 12 km/h.
Let distance be D km.
Time upstream − Time downstream = 4 hours
(D / 12) − (D / 24) = 4 ⇒ D / 24 = 4 ⇒ D = 96 km.

questions.stem: Six years ago, the ratio of the ages of Kunal and Sagar was 6 : 5. Four years hence, the ratio of their ages will be 11 : 10. What is Sagar's present age?
questions.explanation:
Let ages 6 years ago be 6x and 5x.
Present ages = (6x + 6) and (5x + 6).
4 years hence, their ages will be (6x + 10) and (5x + 10).
Given: (6x + 10) / (5x + 10) = 11 / 10
60x + 100 = 55x + 110 ⇒ 5x = 10 ⇒ x = 2.
Sagar's present age = 5x + 6 = 5(2) + 6 = 16 years.

questions.stem: A and B entered into a partnership with initial investments of ₹15,000 and ₹20,000 respectively. After 4 months, A invested an additional ₹5,000, while B withdrew ₹5,000. If the total annual profit was ₹21,000, find A's share of the profit.
A train 240 meters long moving at a speed of 72 km/h crosses a railway platform in 25 seconds. What is the length of the platform?
questions.explanation:
Speed of train in m/s = 72 × (5/18) = 20 m/s.
Total distance covered in 25 seconds = Speed × Time = 20 × 25 = 500 meters.
Total distance = Length of train + Length of platform
500 = 240 + Platform Length
Platform Length = 500 − 240 = 260 meters.

questions.stem: The length and breadth of a rectangular field are in the ratio 5 : 2, and its perimeter is 98 meters. A circular lawn has a radius equal to the breadth of this rectangular field. Find the area of the circular lawn (taking π = 22/7).
questions.explanation:
Perimeter of rectangle = 2(l + b) = 98 ⇒ l + b = 49 m.
Ratio 5 : 2 ⇒ 7x = 49 ⇒ x = 7.
Length = 5 × 7 = 35 m, Breadth = 2 × 7 = 14 m.
Radius of circular lawn r = Breadth = 14 m.
Area of circular lawn = π × r² = (22/7) × 14 × 14 = 616 m².

• All pencils are erasers.
• No erasers is a scales.

Conclusions:

II. No pencils is a scales.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation:

A family consists of seven members: P, Q, R, S, T, U, and V spanning three generations. There are two married couples.

• Q is the only son of P.
• R is the daughter-in-law of P and mother of V.
• S is the sister of Q.
• T is the sister-in-law of R and is unmarried.
• U is the husband of S and father of a daughter.

How is Q related to V?
questions.explanation: P is the grandfather of V, and Q is the only son of P. R is the mother of V and wife of Q. Therefore, Q is the father of V.

questions.stem: How is S related to V?
questions.explanation: S is the sister of Q (V's father). Therefore, S is V's father's sister, which is Paternal Aunt.

questions.stem: How is U related to Q?
questions.explanation: U is the husband of S, who is Q's sister. Therefore, U is Q's sister's husband (Brother-in-law).

questions.stem: A person starts walking from Point A, walks 12 meters towards North to reach Point B. He then turns right (East) and walks 9 meters to reach Point C. He then turns right (South) and walks 12 meters to reach Point D. In which direction and at what shortest distance is Point D from Point A?
questions.explanation: Net North-South displacement = 12m North − 12m South = 0m. Net East displacement = 9m East. Hence, Point D is exactly 9 meters East of Point A.

In the following question, two equations I and II are given. You have to solve both equations and select the appropriate relation:

Equation I: x² − 15x + 56 = 0
Equation II: y² − 9y + 20 = 0
options: x = y or the relationship cannot be established
questions.explanation:
For Eq I: x² − 15x + 56 = 0 ⇒ (x − 7)(x − 8) = 0 ⇒ x = 7, 8.
For Eq II: y² − 9y + 20 = 0 ⇒ (y − 4)(y − 5) = 0 ⇒ y = 4, 5.
Comparing roots:
• 7 > 4 and 7 > 5
• 8 > 4 and 8 > 5
Hence, x > y.

questions.stem: A shopkeeper marks an article 40% above its cost price and sells it after allowing a discount of 15% on the marked price. If he earns a profit of ₹380, what was the cost price of the article?
questions.explanation:
Let Cost Price (CP) = 100x.
Marked Price (MP) = 100x × 1.40 = 140x.
Selling Price (SP) = 140x × (1 − 0.15) = 140x × 0.85 = 119x.
Profit = SP − CP = 119x − 100x = 19x.
Given: 19x = 380 ⇒ x = 20.
Cost Price = 100x = ₹2,000.

questions.stem: The difference between compound interest (compounded annually) and simple interest on a certain principal sum at 10% per annum for 2 years is ₹180. Find the principal sum.
questions.explanation:
For 2 years, the difference between CI and SI is given by:
Difference = P × (R / 100)²
180 = P × (10 / 100)² = P × (1 / 100)
P = 180 × 100 = ₹18,000.

questions.stem: A is 20% more efficient than B. B alone can complete a piece of work in 30 days. Both work together for 6 days, and then B leaves. In how many more days will A alone complete the remaining work?
questions.explanation:
Efficiency ratio of A : B = 120 : 100 = 6 : 5.
Total work = Efficiency of B × Days = 5 × 30 = 150 units.
Combined work done in 6 days = (6 + 5) × 6 = 66 units.
Remaining work = 150 − 66 = 84 units.
Time taken by A alone = 84 ÷ 6 = 14 days.

questions.stem: A vessel contains 80 litres of a mixture of milk and water in the ratio 3 : 1. If 16 litres of this mixture is taken out and replaced with 16 litres of pure water, what is the new ratio of milk to water in the vessel?
questions.explanation:
Initial volume = 80 L (Ratio 3 : 1):
• Milk = (3/4) × 80 = 60 L
• Water = (1/4) × 80 = 20 L
16 L removed:
• Milk removed = (3/4) × 16 = 12 L ⇒ Remaining Milk = 60 − 12 = 48 L
• Water removed = (1/4) × 16 = 4 L ⇒ Remaining Water = 20 − 4 = 16 L
16 L pure water added:
• New Water = 16 + 16 = 32 L
New Ratio of Milk : Water = 48 : 32 = 3 : 2.

questions.stem: Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 hours and Pipe B can fill it in 15 hours. A third pipe C can empty the full tank in 20 hours. If all three pipes are opened simultaneously, in how many hours will the empty tank be completely filled?
questions.explanation:
LCM of 12, 15, and 20 = 60 units (Total tank capacity).
• Efficiency of A = +60/12 = +5 units/h
• Efficiency of B = +60/15 = +4 units/h
• Efficiency of C = −60/20 = −3 units/h
Combined efficiency = 5 + 4 − 3 = 6 units/h.
Time to fill = 60 ÷ 6 = 10 hours.

questions.stem: The speed of a boat in still water is 18 km/h and the speed of the stream is 6 km/h. If the boat takes 4 hours more to travel a certain distance upstream than downstream, find the distance.
questions.explanation:
Downstream speed = 18 + 6 = 24 km/h.
Upstream speed = 18 − 6 = 12 km/h.
Let distance be D km.
Time upstream − Time downstream = 4 hours
(D / 12) − (D / 24) = 4 ⇒ D / 24 = 4 ⇒ D = 96 km.

questions.stem: Six years ago, the ratio of the ages of Kunal and Sagar was 6 : 5. Four years hence, the ratio of their ages will be 11 : 10. What is Sagar's present age?
questions.explanation:
Let ages 6 years ago be 6x and 5x.
Present ages = (6x + 6) and (5x + 6).
4 years hence, their ages will be (6x + 10) and (5x + 10).
Given: (6x + 10) / (5x + 10) = 11 / 10
60x + 100 = 55x + 110 ⇒ 5x = 10 ⇒ x = 2.
Sagar's present age = 5x + 6 = 5(2) + 6 = 16 years.

questions.stem: A and B entered into a partnership with initial investments of ₹15,000 and ₹20,000 respectively. After 4 months, A invested an additional ₹5,000, while B withdrew ₹5,000. If the total annual profit was ₹21,000, find A's share of the profit.
A train 240 meters long moving at a speed of 72 km/h crosses a railway platform in 25 seconds. What is the length of the platform?
questions.explanation:
Speed of train in m/s = 72 × (5/18) = 20 m/s.
Total distance covered in 25 seconds = Speed × Time = 20 × 25 = 500 meters.
Total distance = Length of train + Length of platform
500 = 240 + Platform Length
Platform Length = 500 − 240 = 260 meters.

questions.stem: The length and breadth of a rectangular field are in the ratio 5 : 2, and its perimeter is 98 meters. A circular lawn has a radius equal to the breadth of this rectangular field. Find the area of the circular lawn (taking π = 22/7).
questions.explanation:
Perimeter of rectangle = 2(l + b) = 98 ⇒ l + b = 49 m.
Ratio 5 : 2 ⇒ 7x = 49 ⇒ x = 7.
Length = 5 × 7 = 35 m, Breadth = 2 × 7 = 14 m.
Radius of circular lawn r = Breadth = 14 m.
Area of circular lawn = π × r² = (22/7) × 14 × 14 = 616 m².

Statements:
• Only a few books are papers.
• All papers are notes.
• No notes is a diaries.

Conclusions:
I. Some books are not papers.
II. No papers is a diaries.
options: Either conclusion I or II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation:
1. 'Only a few books are papers' implies both 'Some books are papers' and 'Some books are NOT papers'. Thus, Conclusion I definitely follows.
2. Since all papers are inside notes and no notes is a diaries, there is no intersection between papers and diaries. Hence, Conclusion II follows.

A family consists of seven members: P, Q, R, S, T, U, and V spanning three generations. There are two married couples.
• P is the paternal grandfather of V.
• Q is the only son of P.
• R is the daughter-in-law of P and mother of V.
• S is the sister of Q.
• T is the sister-in-law of R and is unmarried.
• U is the husband of S and father of a daughter.

How is Q related to V?
questions.explanation: P is the grandfather of V, and Q is the only son of P. R is the mother of V and wife of Q. Therefore, Q is the father of V.

questions.stem: How is S related to V?
questions.explanation: S is the sister of Q (V's father). Therefore, S is V's father's sister, which is Paternal Aunt.

questions.stem: How is U related to Q?
questions.explanation: U is the husband of S, who is Q's sister. Therefore, U is Q's sister's husband (Brother-in-law).

questions.stem: A person starts walking from Point A, walks 12 meters towards North to reach Point B. He then turns right (East) and walks 9 meters to reach Point C. In the following question, two equations I and II are given. You have to solve both equations and select the appropriate relation:

Equation I: x² − 15x + 56 = 0
Equation II: y² − 9y + 20 = 0
options: x = y or the relationship cannot be established
questions.explanation:
For Eq I: x² − 15x + 56 = 0 ⇒ (x − 7)(x − 8) = 0 ⇒ x = 7, 8.
For Eq II: y² − 9y + 20 = 0 ⇒ (y − 4)(y − 5) = 0 ⇒ y = 4, 5.
Comparing roots:
• 7 > 4 and 7 > 5
• 8 > 4 and 8 > 5
Hence, x > y.

questions.stem: A shopkeeper marks an article 40% above its cost price and sells it after allowing a discount of 15% on the marked price. If he earns a profit of ₹380, what was the cost price of the article?
questions.explanation:
Let Cost Price (CP) = 100x.
Marked Price (MP) = 100x × 1.40 = 140x.
Selling Price (SP) = 140x × (1 − 0.15) = 140x × 0.85 = 119x.
Profit = SP − CP = 119x − 100x = 19x.
Given: 19x = 380 ⇒ x = 20.
Cost Price = 100x = ₹2,000.

questions.stem: The difference between compound interest (compounded annually) and simple interest on a certain principal sum at 10% per annum for 2 years is ₹180. Find the principal sum.
questions.explanation:
For 2 years, the difference between CI and SI is given by:
Difference = P × (R / 100)²
180 = P × (10 / 100)² = P × (1 / 100)
P = 180 × 100 = ₹18,000.

questions.stem: A is 20% more efficient than B. B alone can complete a piece of work in 30 days. Both work together for 6 days, and then B leaves. In how many more days will A alone complete the remaining work?
questions.explanation:
Efficiency ratio of A : B = 120 : 100 = 6 : 5.
Total work = Efficiency of B × Days = 5 × 30 = 150 units.
Combined work done in 6 days = (6 + 5) × 6 = 66 units.
Remaining work = 150 − 66 = 84 units.
Time taken by A alone = 84 ÷ 6 = 14 days.

questions.stem: A vessel contains 80 litres of a mixture of milk and water in the ratio 3 : 1. If 16 litres of this mixture is taken out and replaced with 16 litres of pure water, what is the new ratio of milk to water in the vessel?
questions.explanation:
Initial volume = 80 L (Ratio 3 : 1):
• Milk = (3/4) × 80 = 60 L
• Water = (1/4) × 80 = 20 L
16 L removed:
• Milk removed = (3/4) × 16 = 12 L ⇒ Remaining Milk = 60 − 12 = 48 L
• Water removed = (1/4) × 16 = 4 L ⇒ Remaining Water = 20 − 4 = 16 L
16 L pure water added:
• New Water = 16 + 16 = 32 L
New Ratio of Milk : Water = 48 : 32 = 3 : 2.

questions.stem: Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 hours and Pipe B can fill it in 15 hours. A third pipe C can empty the full tank in 20 hours. If all three pipes are opened simultaneously, in how many hours will the empty tank be completely filled?
questions.explanation:
LCM of 12, 15, and 20 = 60 units (Total tank capacity).
• Efficiency of A = +60/12 = +5 units/h
• Efficiency of B = +60/15 = +4 units/h
• Efficiency of C = −60/20 = −3 units/h
Combined efficiency = 5 + 4 − 3 = 6 units/h.
Time to fill = 60 ÷ 6 = 10 hours.

questions.stem: The speed of a boat in still water is 18 km/h and the speed of the stream is 6 km/h. If the boat takes 4 hours more to travel a certain distance upstream than downstream, find the distance.
questions.explanation:
Downstream speed = 18 + 6 = 24 km/h.
Upstream speed = 18 − 6 = 12 km/h.
Let distance be D km.
Time upstream − Time downstream = 4 hours
(D / 12) − (D / 24) = 4 ⇒ D / 24 = 4 ⇒ D = 96 km.

questions.stem: Six years ago, the ratio of the ages of Kunal and Sagar was 6 : 5. Four years hence, the ratio of their ages will be 11 : 10. What is Sagar's present age?
questions.explanation:
Let ages 6 years ago be 6x and 5x.
Present ages = (6x + 6) and (5x + 6).
4 years hence, their ages will be (6x + 10) and (5x + 10).
Given: (6x + 10) / (5x + 10) = 11 / 10

A train 240 meters long moving at a speed of 72 km/h crosses a railway platform in 25 seconds. What is the length of the platform?
questions.explanation:
Speed of train in m/s = 72 × (5/18) = 20 m/s.
Total distance covered in 25 seconds = Speed × Time = 20 × 25 = 500 meters.
Total distance = Length of train + Length of platform
500 = 240 + Platform Length
Platform Length = 500 − 240 = 260 meters.

questions.stem: The length and breadth of a rectangular field are in the ratio 5 : 2, and its perimeter is 98 meters. A circular lawn has a radius equal to the breadth of this rectangular field. Find the area of the circular lawn (taking π = 22/7).
questions.explanation:
Perimeter of rectangle = 2(l + b) = 98 ⇒ l + b = 49 m.
Ratio 5 : 2 ⇒ 7x = 49 ⇒ x = 7.
Length = 5 × 7 = 35 m, Breadth = 2 × 7 = 14 m.
Radius of circular lawn r = Breadth = 14 m.
Area of circular lawn = π × r² = (22/7) × 14 × 14 = 616 m².

questions.stem:
In the question below, statements are given followed by two conclusions. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the given statements.

Statements:
• Only a few cities are towns.
• All towns are villages.
• No villages is a districts.

Conclusions:
I. Some cities are not towns.
II. No towns is a districts.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation:
1. 'Only a few cities are towns' implies both 'Some cities are towns' and 'Some cities are NOT towns'. Thus, Conclusion I definitely follows.
2. Since all towns are inside villages and no villages is a districts, there is no intersection between towns and districts. Hence, Conclusion II follows.

questions.stem:
In the question below, statements are given followed by two conclusions. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the given statements.

Statements:
• Only a few cities are towns.
• Few towns are villages.
• All villages are districts.

Conclusions:
I. All cities being towns is a possibility.
II. Some towns are districts.
options: Either conclusion I or II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation:
1. 'Only a few cities are towns' strictly forbids all cities from being towns. Hence, Conclusion I is NOT a valid possibility.
2. Since some towns are villages and all villages are districts, the common portion of towns and villages must also be districts. Hence, Conclusion II definitely follows.

questions.stem:
In the question below, statements are given followed by two conclusions. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the given statements.

options: Both conclusions I and II follow

questions.explanation:

2. There is no negative restriction between towns and districts. Hence, all towns being districts is a valid possibility. Both follow.

In the following question, two equations I and II are given. You have to solve both equations and select the appropriate relation:

Equation I: x² − 15x + 56 = 0
Equation II: y² − 9y + 20 = 0
options: x = y or the relationship cannot be established
questions.explanation:
For Eq I: x² − 15x + 56 = 0 ⇒ (x − 7)(x − 8) = 0 ⇒ x = 7, 8.
For Eq II: y² − 9y + 20 = 0 ⇒ (y − 4)(y − 5) = 0 ⇒ y = 4, 5.
Comparing roots:
• 7 > 4 and 7 > 5
• 8 > 4 and 8 > 5
Hence, x > y.

questions.stem:
In the following question, two equations I and II are given. You have to solve both equations and select the appropriate relation:

Equation I: x² − 3x − 10 = 0
Equation II: y² − 7y + 12 = 0
options: x = y or the relationship cannot be established
questions.explanation:
For Eq I: x² − 3x − 10 = 0 ⇒ (x − 5)(x + 2) = 0 ⇒ x = 5, −2.
For Eq II: y² − 7y + 12 = 0 ⇒ (y − 3)(y − 4) = 0 ⇒ y = 3, 4.
Comparing roots:
• When x = 5: 5 > 3 and 5 > 4 (x > y)
• When x = −2: −2 < 3 and −2 < 4 (x < y)
Since opposite relationships hold, relationship cannot be established.

questions.stem:
What will come in place of the question mark (?) in the following number series?
12, 7, 9, 16.5, 37, ?

What will come in place of (?) in the following number series?
15, 16, 24, 51, 115, ?
questions.explanation:
The difference between consecutive terms is cubes of consecutive integers:
• 16 − 15 = 1 (1³)
• 24 − 16 = 8 (2³)
• 51 − 24 = 27 (3³)
• 115 − 51 = 64 (4³)
• Next term = 115 + 5³ = 115 + 125 = 240.

questions.stem:

8, 14, 26, 44, 68, ?

Identify the missing term in the sequence:
5, 9, 16, 29, 54, ?

Find the WRONG number in the given series:
4, 11, 25, 53, 108, 221
questions.explanation:
The pattern is (term × 2 + 3):
• 4 × 2 + 3 = 11
• 11 × 2 + 3 = 25
• 25 × 2 + 3 = 53
• 53 × 2 + 3 = 109 (Instead of 108)
• 109 × 2 + 3 = 221
Therefore, 108 is the wrong number in the series.

questions.stem: A shopkeeper marks an article 40% above its cost price and sells it after allowing a discount of 15% on the marked price. If he earns a profit of ₹380, what was the cost price of the article?
questions.explanation:
Let Cost Price (CP) = 100x.
Marked Price (MP) = 100x × 1.40 = 140x.
Selling Price (SP) = 140x × (1 − 0.15) = 140x × 0.85 = 119x.
Profit = SP − CP = 119x − 100x = 19x.
Given: 19x = 380 ⇒ x = 20.
Cost Price = 100x = ₹2,000.

questions.stem: The difference between compound interest (compounded annually) and simple interest on a certain principal sum at 10% per annum for 2 years is ₹180. Find the principal sum.
questions.explanation:
For 2 years, the difference between CI and SI is given by:
Difference = P × (R / 100)²
180 = P × (10 / 100)² = P × (1 / 100)
P = 180 × 100 = ₹18,000.

questions.stem: A is 20% more efficient than B. B alone can complete a piece of work in 30 days. Both work together for 6 days, and then B leaves. In how many more days will A alone complete the remaining work?
questions.explanation:
Efficiency ratio of A : B = 120 : 100 = 6 : 5.
Total work = Efficiency of B × Days = 5 × 30 = 150 units.
Combined work done in 6 days = (6 + 5) × 6 = 66 units.
Remaining work = 150 − 66 = 84 units.
Time taken by A alone = 84 ÷ 6 = 14 days.

questions.stem: A vessel contains 80 litres of a mixture of milk and water in the ratio 3 : 1. If 16 litres of this mixture is taken out and replaced with 16 litres of pure water, what is the new ratio of milk to water in the vessel?
questions.explanation:
Initial volume = 80 L (Ratio 3 : 1):
• Milk = (3/4) × 80 = 60 L
• Water = (1/4) × 80 = 20 L
16 L removed:
• Milk removed = (3/4) × 16 = 12 L ⇒ Remaining Milk = 60 − 12 = 48 L
• Water removed = (1/4) × 16 = 4 L ⇒ Remaining Water = 20 − 4 = 16 L
16 L pure water added:
• New Water = 16 + 16 = 32 L
New Ratio of Milk : Water = 48 : 32 = 3 : 2.

questions.stem: Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 hours and Pipe B can fill it in 15 hours. A third pipe C can empty the full tank in 20 hours. If all three pipes are opened simultaneously, in how many hours will the empty tank be completely filled?
questions.explanation:
LCM of 12, 15, and 20 = 60 units (Total tank capacity).
• Efficiency of A = +60/12 = +5 units/h
• Efficiency of B = +60/15 = +4 units/h
• Efficiency of C = −60/20 = −3 units/h
Combined efficiency = 5 + 4 − 3 = 6 units/h.
Time to fill = 60 ÷ 6 = 10 hours.

questions.stem: The speed of a boat in still water is 18 km/h and the speed of the stream is 6 km/h. If the boat takes 4 hours more to travel a certain distance upstream than downstream, find the distance.
questions.explanation:
Downstream speed = 18 + 6 = 24 km/h.
Upstream speed = 18 − 6 = 12 km/h.
Let distance be D km.
Time upstream − Time downstream = 4 hours
(D / 12) − (D / 24) = 4 ⇒ D / 24 = 4 ⇒ D = 96 km.

questions.stem: Six years ago, the ratio of the ages of Kunal and Sagar was 6 : 5. Four years hence, the ratio of their ages will be 11 : 10. What is Sagar's present age?
questions.explanation:
Let ages 6 years ago be 6x and 5x.
Present ages = (6x + 6) and (5x + 6).
4 years hence, their ages will be (6x + 10) and (5x + 10).
Given: (6x + 10) / (5x + 10) = 11 / 10
60x + 100 = 55x + 110 ⇒ 5x = 10 ⇒ x = 2.
Sagar's present age = 5x + 6 = 5(2) + 6 = 16 years.

questions.stem: A and B entered into a partnership with initial investments of ₹15,000 and ₹20,000 respectively. After 4 months, A invested an additional ₹5,000, while B withdrew ₹5,000. If the total annual profit was ₹21,000, find A's share of the profit.
A train 240 meters long moving at a speed of 72 km/h crosses a railway platform in 25 seconds. What is the length of the platform?
questions.explanation:
Speed of train in m/s = 72 × (5/18) = 20 m/s.
Total distance covered in 25 seconds = Speed × Time = 20 × 25 = 500 meters.
Total distance = Length of train + Length of platform
500 = 240 + Platform Length
Platform Length = 500 − 240 = 260 meters.

questions.stem: The length and breadth of a rectangular field are in the ratio 5 : 2, and its perimeter is 98 meters. A circular lawn has a radius equal to the breadth of this rectangular field. Find the area of the circular lawn (taking π = 22/7).
questions.explanation:
Perimeter of rectangle = 2(l + b) = 98 ⇒ l + b = 49 m.
Ratio 5 : 2 ⇒ 7x = 49 ⇒ x = 7.
Length = 5 × 7 = 35 m, Breadth = 2 × 7 = 14 m.
Radius of circular lawn r = Breadth = 14 m.
Area of circular lawn = π × r² = (22/7) × 14 × 14 = 616 m².

In the following question, two equations I and II are given. You have to solve both equations and select the appropriate relation:

Equation I: x² − 15x + 56 = 0
Equation II: y² − 9y + 20 = 0
options: x = y or the relationship cannot be established
questions.explanation:
For Eq I: x² − 15x + 56 = 0 ⇒ (x − 7)(x − 8) = 0 ⇒ x = 7, 8.
For Eq II: y² − 9y + 20 = 0 ⇒ (y − 4)(y − 5) = 0 ⇒ y = 4, 5.
Comparing roots:
• 7 > 4 and 7 > 5
• 8 > 4 and 8 > 5
Hence, x > y.

questions.stem: A shopkeeper marks an article 40% above its cost price and sells it after allowing a discount of 15% on the marked price. If he earns a profit of ₹380, what was the cost price of the article?
questions.explanation:
Let Cost Price (CP) = 100x.
Marked Price (MP) = 100x × 1.40 = 140x.
Selling Price (SP) = 140x × (1 − 0.15) = 140x × 0.85 = 119x.
Profit = SP − CP = 119x − 100x = 19x.
Given: 19x = 380 ⇒ x = 20.
Cost Price = 100x = ₹2,000.

questions.stem: The difference between compound interest (compounded annually) and simple interest on a certain principal sum at 10% per annum for 2 years is ₹180. Find the principal sum.
questions.explanation:
For 2 years, the difference between CI and SI is given by:
Difference = P × (R / 100)²
180 = P × (10 / 100)² = P × (1 / 100)
P = 180 × 100 = ₹18,000.

questions.stem: A is 20% more efficient than B. B alone can complete a piece of work in 30 days. Both work together for 6 days, and then B leaves. In how many more days will A alone complete the remaining work?
questions.explanation:
Efficiency ratio of A : B = 120 : 100 = 6 : 5.
Total work = Efficiency of B × Days = 5 × 30 = 150 units.
Combined work done in 6 days = (6 + 5) × 6 = 66 units.
Remaining work = 150 − 66 = 84 units.
Time taken by A alone = 84 ÷ 6 = 14 days.

questions.stem: A vessel contains 80 litres of a mixture of milk and water in the ratio 3 : 1. If 16 litres of this mixture is taken out and replaced with 16 litres of pure water, what is the new ratio of milk to water in the vessel?
questions.explanation:
Initial volume = 80 L (Ratio 3 : 1):
• Milk = (3/4) × 80 = 60 L
• Water = (1/4) × 80 = 20 L
16 L removed:
• Milk removed = (3/4) × 16 = 12 L ⇒ Remaining Milk = 60 − 12 = 48 L
• Water removed = (1/4) × 16 = 4 L ⇒ Remaining Water = 20 − 4 = 16 L
16 L pure water added:
• New Water = 16 + 16 = 32 L
New Ratio of Milk : Water = 48 : 32 = 3 : 2.

questions.stem: Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 hours and Pipe B can fill it in 15 hours. A third pipe C can empty the full tank in 20 hours. If all three pipes are opened simultaneously, in how many hours will the empty tank be completely filled?
questions.explanation:
LCM of 12, 15, and 20 = 60 units (Total tank capacity).
• Efficiency of A = +60/12 = +5 units/h
• Efficiency of B = +60/15 = +4 units/h
• Efficiency of C = −60/20 = −3 units/h
Combined efficiency = 5 + 4 − 3 = 6 units/h.
Time to fill = 60 ÷ 6 = 10 hours.

questions.stem: The speed of a boat in still water is 18 km/h and the speed of the stream is 6 km/h. If the boat takes 4 hours more to travel a certain distance upstream than downstream, find the distance.
questions.explanation:
Downstream speed = 18 + 6 = 24 km/h.
Upstream speed = 18 − 6 = 12 km/h.
Let distance be D km.
Time upstream − Time downstream = 4 hours
(D / 12) − (D / 24) = 4 ⇒ D / 24 = 4 ⇒ D = 96 km.

questions.stem: Six years ago, the ratio of the ages of Kunal and Sagar was 6 : 5. Four years hence, the ratio of their ages will be 11 : 10. What is Sagar's present age?
questions.explanation:
Let ages 6 years ago be 6x and 5x.
Present ages = (6x + 6) and (5x + 6).
4 years hence, their ages will be (6x + 10) and (5x + 10).
Given: (6x + 10) / (5x + 10) = 11 / 10
60x + 100 = 55x + 110 ⇒ 5x = 10 ⇒ x = 2.
Sagar's present age = 5x + 6 = 5(2) + 6 = 16 years.

questions.stem: A and B entered into a partnership with initial investments of ₹15,000 and ₹20,000 respectively. After 4 months, A invested an additional ₹5,000, while B withdrew ₹5,000. If the total annual profit was ₹21,000, find A's share of the profit.
A train 240 meters long moving at a speed of 72 km/h crosses a railway platform in 25 seconds. What is the length of the platform?
questions.explanation:
Speed of train in m/s = 72 × (5/18) = 20 m/s.
Total distance covered in 25 seconds = Speed × Time = 20 × 25 = 500 meters.
Total distance = Length of train + Length of platform
500 = 240 + Platform Length
Platform Length = 500 − 240 = 260 meters.

questions.stem: The length and breadth of a rectangular field are in the ratio 5 : 2, and its perimeter is 98 meters. A circular lawn has a radius equal to the breadth of this rectangular field. Find the area of the circular lawn (taking π = 22/7).
questions.explanation:
Perimeter of rectangle = 2(l + b) = 98 ⇒ l + b = 49 m.
Ratio 5 : 2 ⇒ 7x = 49 ⇒ x = 7.
Length = 5 × 7 = 35 m, Breadth = 2 × 7 = 14 m.
Radius of circular lawn r = Breadth = 14 m.
Area of circular lawn = π × r² = (22/7) × 14 × 14 = 616 m².

questions.stem:
In the question below, statements are given followed by two conclusions. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the given statements.

Statements:
• Only a few rivers are lakes.
• All lakes are oceans.
• No oceans is a ponds.

Conclusions:
I. Some rivers are not lakes.
II. No lakes is a ponds.
options: Either conclusion I or II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation:
1. 'Only a few rivers are lakes' implies both 'Some rivers are lakes' and 'Some rivers are NOT lakes'. Thus, Conclusion I definitely follows.
2. Since all lakes are inside oceans and no oceans is a ponds, there is no intersection between lakes and ponds. Hence, Conclusion II follows.

questions.stem:

Statements:
• Only a few rivers are lakes.
• Few lakes are oceans.
• All oceans are ponds.

Conclusions:
I. All rivers being lakes is a possibility.
II. Some lakes are ponds.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation:
1. 'Only a few rivers are lakes' strictly forbids all rivers from being lakes. Hence, Conclusion I is NOT a valid possibility.
2. Since some lakes are oceans and all oceans are ponds, the common portion of lakes and oceans must also be ponds. Hence, Conclusion II definitely follows.

Either conclusion I or II is true
questions.explanation:

questions.stem:

Either conclusion I or II is true

questions.stem: A person starts walking from Point A, walks 12 meters towards North to reach Point B. He then turns right (East) and walks 9 meters to reach Point C. In the following question, two equations I and II are given. You have to solve both equations and select the appropriate relation:

Equation I: x² − 15x + 56 = 0
Equation II: y² − 9y + 20 = 0
options: x = y or the relationship cannot be established
questions.explanation:
For Eq I: x² − 15x + 56 = 0 ⇒ (x − 7)(x − 8) = 0 ⇒ x = 7, 8.
For Eq II: y² − 9y + 20 = 0 ⇒ (y − 4)(y − 5) = 0 ⇒ y = 4, 5.
Comparing roots:
• 7 > 4 and 7 > 5
• 8 > 4 and 8 > 5
Hence, x > y.

Comparing roots:

• 3 < 6 and 3 < 7
Hence, x < y.

questions.stem: A shopkeeper marks an article 40% above its cost price and sells it after allowing a discount of 15% on the marked price. If he earns a profit of ₹380, what was the cost price of the article?
questions.explanation:
Let Cost Price (CP) = 100x.
Marked Price (MP) = 100x × 1.40 = 140x.
Selling Price (SP) = 140x × (1 − 0.15) = 140x × 0.85 = 119x.
Profit = SP − CP = 119x − 100x = 19x.
Given: 19x = 380 ⇒ x = 20.
Cost Price = 100x = ₹2,000.

questions.stem: The difference between compound interest (compounded annually) and simple interest on a certain principal sum at 10% per annum for 2 years is ₹180. Find the principal sum.
questions.explanation:
For 2 years, the difference between CI and SI is given by:
Difference = P × (R / 100)²
180 = P × (10 / 100)² = P × (1 / 100)
P = 180 × 100 = ₹18,000.

questions.stem: A is 20% more efficient than B. B alone can complete a piece of work in 30 days. Both work together for 6 days, and then B leaves. In how many more days will A alone complete the remaining work?
questions.explanation:
Efficiency ratio of A : B = 120 : 100 = 6 : 5.
Total work = Efficiency of B × Days = 5 × 30 = 150 units.
Combined work done in 6 days = (6 + 5) × 6 = 66 units.
Remaining work = 150 − 66 = 84 units.
Time taken by A alone = 84 ÷ 6 = 14 days.

questions.stem: A vessel contains 80 litres of a mixture of milk and water in the ratio 3 : 1. If 16 litres of this mixture is taken out and replaced with 16 litres of pure water, what is the new ratio of milk to water in the vessel?
questions.explanation:
Initial volume = 80 L (Ratio 3 : 1):
• Milk = (3/4) × 80 = 60 L
• Water = (1/4) × 80 = 20 L
16 L removed:
• Milk removed = (3/4) × 16 = 12 L ⇒ Remaining Milk = 60 − 12 = 48 L
• Water removed = (1/4) × 16 = 4 L ⇒ Remaining Water = 20 − 4 = 16 L
16 L pure water added:
• New Water = 16 + 16 = 32 L
New Ratio of Milk : Water = 48 : 32 = 3 : 2.

questions.stem: Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 hours and Pipe B can fill it in 15 hours. A third pipe C can empty the full tank in 20 hours. If all three pipes are opened simultaneously, in how many hours will the empty tank be completely filled?
questions.explanation:
LCM of 12, 15, and 20 = 60 units (Total tank capacity).
• Efficiency of A = +60/12 = +5 units/h
• Efficiency of B = +60/15 = +4 units/h
• Efficiency of C = −60/20 = −3 units/h
Combined efficiency = 5 + 4 − 3 = 6 units/h.
Time to fill = 60 ÷ 6 = 10 hours.

questions.stem: The speed of a boat in still water is 18 km/h and the speed of the stream is 6 km/h. If the boat takes 4 hours more to travel a certain distance upstream than downstream, find the distance.
questions.explanation:
Downstream speed = 18 + 6 = 24 km/h.
Upstream speed = 18 − 6 = 12 km/h.
Let distance be D km.
Time upstream − Time downstream = 4 hours
(D / 12) − (D / 24) = 4 ⇒ D / 24 = 4 ⇒ D = 96 km.

questions.stem: Six years ago, the ratio of the ages of Kunal and Sagar was 6 : 5. Four years hence, the ratio of their ages will be 11 : 10. What is Sagar's present age?
questions.explanation:
Let ages 6 years ago be 6x and 5x.
Present ages = (6x + 6) and (5x + 6).
4 years hence, their ages will be (6x + 10) and (5x + 10).
Given: (6x + 10) / (5x + 10) = 11 / 10
60x + 100 = 55x + 110 ⇒ 5x = 10 ⇒ x = 2.
Sagar's present age = 5x + 6 = 5(2) + 6 = 16 years.

questions.stem: A and B entered into a partnership with initial investments of ₹15,000 and ₹20,000 respectively. After 4 months, A invested an additional ₹5,000, while B withdrew ₹5,000. If the total annual profit was ₹21,000, find A's share of the profit.
A train 240 meters long moving at a speed of 72 km/h crosses a railway platform in 25 seconds. What is the length of the platform?
questions.explanation:
Speed of train in m/s = 72 × (5/18) = 20 m/s.
Total distance covered in 25 seconds = Speed × Time = 20 × 25 = 500 meters.
Total distance = Length of train + Length of platform
500 = 240 + Platform Length
Platform Length = 500 − 240 = 260 meters.

questions.stem: The length and breadth of a rectangular field are in the ratio 5 : 2, and its perimeter is 98 meters. A circular lawn has a radius equal to the breadth of this rectangular field. Find the area of the circular lawn (taking π = 22/7).
questions.explanation:
Perimeter of rectangle = 2(l + b) = 98 ⇒ l + b = 49 m.
Ratio 5 : 2 ⇒ 7x = 49 ⇒ x = 7.
Length = 5 × 7 = 35 m, Breadth = 2 × 7 = 14 m.
Radius of circular lawn r = Breadth = 14 m.
Area of circular lawn = π × r² = (22/7) × 14 × 14 = 616 m².

questions.stem:
In the question below, statements are given followed by two conclusions. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the given statements.

Statements:
• Only a few cars are buses.
• All buses are trains.
• No trains is a trucks.

Conclusions:
I. Some cars are not buses.
II. No buses is a trucks.
options: Either conclusion I or II follows
Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation:
1. 'Only a few cars are buses' implies both 'Some cars are buses' and 'Some cars are NOT buses'. Thus, Conclusion I definitely follows.
2. Since all buses are inside trains and no trains is a trucks, there is no intersection between buses and trucks. Hence, Conclusion II follows.

questions.stem:
Study the information carefully to answer the questions:
A family consists of seven members: P, Q, R, S, T, U, and V spanning three generations. There are two married couples.

• Q is the only son of P.
• R is the daughter-in-law of P and mother of V.
• S is the sister of Q.
• T is the sister-in-law of R and is unmarried.
• U is the husband of S and father of a daughter.

How is Q related to V?
questions.explanation: P is the grandfather of V, and Q is the only son of P. R is the mother of V and wife of Q. Therefore, Q is the father of V.

questions.stem: How is S related to V?
questions.explanation: S is the sister of Q (V's father). Therefore, S is V's father's sister, which is Paternal Aunt.

questions.stem: How is U related to Q?
questions.explanation: U is the husband of S, who is Q's sister. Therefore, U is Q's sister's husband (Brother-in-law).

questions.stem: A person starts walking from Point A, walks 12 meters towards North to reach Point B. He then turns right (East) and walks 9 meters to reach Point C. He then turns right (South) and walks 12 meters to reach Point D. In which direction and at what shortest distance is Point D from Point A?
questions.explanation: Net North-South displacement = 12m North − 12m South = 0m. Net East displacement = 9m East. Hence, Point D is exactly 9 meters East of Point A.

In the following question, two equations I and II are given. You have to solve both equations and select the appropriate relation:

Equation I: x² − 15x + 56 = 0
Equation II: y² − 9y + 20 = 0
options: x = y or the relationship cannot be established
questions.explanation:
For Eq I: x² − 15x + 56 = 0 ⇒ (x − 7)(x − 8) = 0 ⇒ x = 7, 8.
For Eq II: y² − 9y + 20 = 0 ⇒ (y − 4)(y − 5) = 0 ⇒ y = 4, 5.
Comparing roots:
• 7 > 4 and 7 > 5
• 8 > 4 and 8 > 5
Hence, x > y.

questions.stem:

Equation II: y² − 13y + 42 = 0
options: x = y or the relationship cannot be established
questions.explanation:
For Eq I: x² − 5x + 6 = 0 ⇒ (x − 2)(x − 3) = 0 ⇒ x = 2, 3.
For Eq II: y² − 13y + 42 = 0 ⇒ (y − 6)(y − 7) = 0 ⇒ y = 6, 7.
Comparing roots:
• 2 < 6 and 2 < 7
• 3 < 6 and 3 < 7
Hence, x < y.

12, 7, 9, 16.5, 37, ?

What will come in place of (?) in the following number series?

questions.explanation:
The difference between consecutive terms is cubes of consecutive integers:
• 16 − 15 = 1 (1³)
• 24 − 16 = 8 (2³)

• 115 − 51 = 64 (4³)

Identify the missing term in the sequence:
5, 9, 16, 29, 54, ?

Find the WRONG number in the given series:
4, 11, 25, 53, 108, 221
questions.explanation:
The pattern is (term × 2 + 3):
• 4 × 2 + 3 = 11
• 11 × 2 + 3 = 25
• 25 × 2 + 3 = 53
• 53 × 2 + 3 = 109 (Instead of 108)
• 109 × 2 + 3 = 221
Therefore, 108 is the wrong number in the series.

questions.stem: A shopkeeper marks an article 40% above its cost price and sells it after allowing a discount of 15% on the marked price. If he earns a profit of ₹380, what was the cost price of the article?
questions.explanation:
Let Cost Price (CP) = 100x.
Marked Price (MP) = 100x × 1.40 = 140x.
Selling Price (SP) = 140x × (1 − 0.15) = 140x × 0.85 = 119x.
Profit = SP − CP = 119x − 100x = 19x.
Given: 19x = 380 ⇒ x = 20.
Cost Price = 100x = ₹2,000.

questions.stem: The difference between compound interest (compounded annually) and simple interest on a certain principal sum at 10% per annum for 2 years is ₹180. Find the principal sum.
questions.explanation:
For 2 years, the difference between CI and SI is given by:
Difference = P × (R / 100)²
180 = P × (10 / 100)² = P × (1 / 100)
P = 180 × 100 = ₹18,000.

questions.stem: A is 20% more efficient than B. B alone can complete a piece of work in 30 days. Both work together for 6 days, and then B leaves. In how many more days will A alone complete the remaining work?
questions.explanation:
Efficiency ratio of A : B = 120 : 100 = 6 : 5.
Total work = Efficiency of B × Days = 5 × 30 = 150 units.
Combined work done in 6 days = (6 + 5) × 6 = 66 units.
Remaining work = 150 − 66 = 84 units.
Time taken by A alone = 84 ÷ 6 = 14 days.

questions.stem: A vessel contains 80 litres of a mixture of milk and water in the ratio 3 : 1. If 16 litres of this mixture is taken out and replaced with 16 litres of pure water, what is the new ratio of milk to water in the vessel?
questions.explanation:
Initial volume = 80 L (Ratio 3 : 1):
• Milk = (3/4) × 80 = 60 L
• Water = (1/4) × 80 = 20 L
16 L removed:
• Milk removed = (3/4) × 16 = 12 L ⇒ Remaining Milk = 60 − 12 = 48 L
• Water removed = (1/4) × 16 = 4 L ⇒ Remaining Water = 20 − 4 = 16 L
16 L pure water added:
• New Water = 16 + 16 = 32 L
New Ratio of Milk : Water = 48 : 32 = 3 : 2.

questions.stem: Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 hours and Pipe B can fill it in 15 hours. A third pipe C can empty the full tank in 20 hours. If all three pipes are opened simultaneously, in how many hours will the empty tank be completely filled?
questions.explanation:
LCM of 12, 15, and 20 = 60 units (Total tank capacity).
• Efficiency of A = +60/12 = +5 units/h
• Efficiency of B = +60/15 = +4 units/h
• Efficiency of C = −60/20 = −3 units/h
Combined efficiency = 5 + 4 − 3 = 6 units/h.
Time to fill = 60 ÷ 6 = 10 hours.

questions.stem: The speed of a boat in still water is 18 km/h and the speed of the stream is 6 km/h. If the boat takes 4 hours more to travel a certain distance upstream than downstream, find the distance.
questions.explanation:
Downstream speed = 18 + 6 = 24 km/h.
Upstream speed = 18 − 6 = 12 km/h.
Let distance be D km.
Time upstream − Time downstream = 4 hours
(D / 12) − (D / 24) = 4 ⇒ D / 24 = 4 ⇒ D = 96 km.

questions.stem: Six years ago, the ratio of the ages of Kunal and Sagar was 6 : 5. Four years hence, the ratio of their ages will be 11 : 10. What is Sagar's present age?
questions.explanation:
Let ages 6 years ago be 6x and 5x.
Present ages = (6x + 6) and (5x + 6).
4 years hence, their ages will be (6x + 10) and (5x + 10).
Given: (6x + 10) / (5x + 10) = 11 / 10
60x + 100 = 55x + 110 ⇒ 5x = 10 ⇒ x = 2.
Sagar's present age = 5x + 6 = 5(2) + 6 = 16 years.

questions.stem: A and B entered into a partnership with initial investments of ₹15,000 and ₹20,000 respectively. After 4 months, A invested an additional ₹5,000, while B withdrew ₹5,000. If the total annual profit was ₹21,000, find A's share of the profit.
A train 240 meters long moving at a speed of 72 km/h crosses a railway platform in 25 seconds. What is the length of the platform?
questions.explanation:
Speed of train in m/s = 72 × (5/18) = 20 m/s.
Total distance covered in 25 seconds = Speed × Time = 20 × 25 = 500 meters.
Total distance = Length of train + Length of platform
500 = 240 + Platform Length
Platform Length = 500 − 240 = 260 meters.

questions.stem: The length and breadth of a rectangular field are in the ratio 5 : 2, and its perimeter is 98 meters. A circular lawn has a radius equal to the breadth of this rectangular field. Find the area of the circular lawn (taking π = 22/7).
questions.explanation:
Perimeter of rectangle = 2(l + b) = 98 ⇒ l + b = 49 m.
Ratio 5 : 2 ⇒ 7x = 49 ⇒ x = 7.
Length = 5 × 7 = 35 m, Breadth = 2 × 7 = 14 m.
Radius of circular lawn r = Breadth = 14 m.
Area of circular lawn = π × r² = (22/7) × 14 × 14 = 616 m².

questions.stem:
In the question below, statements are given followed by two conclusions. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the given statements.

Statements:
• Only a few fruits are apples.
• All apples are mangoes.
• No mangoes is a oranges.

Conclusions:
I. Some fruits are not apples.
II. No apples is a oranges.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows
questions.explanation:
1. 'Only a few fruits are apples' implies both 'Some fruits are apples' and 'Some fruits are NOT apples'. Thus, Conclusion I definitely follows.
2. Since all apples are inside mangoes and no mangoes is a oranges, there is no intersection between apples and oranges. Hence, Conclusion II follows.

Both conclusions I and II follow

2. Since some apples are mangoes and all mangoes are oranges, the common portion of apples and mangoes must also be oranges. Hence, Conclusion II definitely follows.

questions.explanation:

questions.stem:

questions.stem:

In the following question, two equations I and II are given. You have to solve both equations and select the appropriate relation:

Equation II: y² − 9y + 20 = 0

questions.stem: A shopkeeper marks an article 40% above its cost price and sells it after allowing a discount of 15% on the marked price. If he earns a profit of ₹380, what was the cost price of the article?
questions.explanation:
Let Cost Price (CP) = 100x.
Marked Price (MP) = 100x × 1.40 = 140x.
Selling Price (SP) = 140x × (1 − 0.15) = 140x × 0.85 = 119x.
Profit = SP − CP = 119x − 100x = 19x.
Given: 19x = 380 ⇒ x = 20.
Cost Price = 100x = ₹2,000.

questions.stem: The difference between compound interest (compounded annually) and simple interest on a certain principal sum at 10% per annum for 2 years is ₹180. Find the principal sum.
questions.explanation:
For 2 years, the difference between CI and SI is given by:
Difference = P × (R / 100)²
180 = P × (10 / 100)² = P × (1 / 100)
P = 180 × 100 = ₹18,000.

questions.stem: A is 20% more efficient than B. B alone can complete a piece of work in 30 days. Both work together for 6 days, and then B leaves. In how many more days will A alone complete the remaining work?
questions.explanation:
Efficiency ratio of A : B = 120 : 100 = 6 : 5.
Total work = Efficiency of B × Days = 5 × 30 = 150 units.
Combined work done in 6 days = (6 + 5) × 6 = 66 units.
Remaining work = 150 − 66 = 84 units.
Time taken by A alone = 84 ÷ 6 = 14 days.

questions.stem: A vessel contains 80 litres of a mixture of milk and water in the ratio 3 : 1. If 16 litres of this mixture is taken out and replaced with 16 litres of pure water, what is the new ratio of milk to water in the vessel?
questions.explanation:
Initial volume = 80 L (Ratio 3 : 1):
• Milk = (3/4) × 80 = 60 L
• Water = (1/4) × 80 = 20 L
16 L removed:
• Milk removed = (3/4) × 16 = 12 L ⇒ Remaining Milk = 60 − 12 = 48 L
• Water removed = (1/4) × 16 = 4 L ⇒ Remaining Water = 20 − 4 = 16 L
16 L pure water added:
• New Water = 16 + 16 = 32 L
New Ratio of Milk : Water = 48 : 32 = 3 : 2.

questions.stem: Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 hours and Pipe B can fill it in 15 hours. A third pipe C can empty the full tank in 20 hours. If all three pipes are opened simultaneously, in how many hours will the empty tank be completely filled?
questions.explanation:
LCM of 12, 15, and 20 = 60 units (Total tank capacity).
• Efficiency of A = +60/12 = +5 units/h
• Efficiency of B = +60/15 = +4 units/h
• Efficiency of C = −60/20 = −3 units/h
Combined efficiency = 5 + 4 − 3 = 6 units/h.
Time to fill = 60 ÷ 6 = 10 hours.

questions.stem: The speed of a boat in still water is 18 km/h and the speed of the stream is 6 km/h. If the boat takes 4 hours more to travel a certain distance upstream than downstream, find the distance.
questions.explanation:
Downstream speed = 18 + 6 = 24 km/h.
Upstream speed = 18 − 6 = 12 km/h.
Let distance be D km.
Time upstream − Time downstream = 4 hours
(D / 12) − (D / 24) = 4 ⇒ D / 24 = 4 ⇒ D = 96 km.

questions.stem: Six years ago, the ratio of the ages of Kunal and Sagar was 6 : 5. Four years hence, the ratio of their ages will be 11 : 10. What is Sagar's present age?
questions.explanation:
Let ages 6 years ago be 6x and 5x.
Present ages = (6x + 6) and (5x + 6).
4 years hence, their ages will be (6x + 10) and (5x + 10).
Given: (6x + 10) / (5x + 10) = 11 / 10
60x + 100 = 55x + 110 ⇒ 5x = 10 ⇒ x = 2.
Sagar's present age = 5x + 6 = 5(2) + 6 = 16 years.

questions.stem: A and B entered into a partnership with initial investments of ₹15,000 and ₹20,000 respectively. After 4 months, A invested an additional ₹5,000, while B withdrew ₹5,000. If the total annual profit was ₹21,000, find A's share of the profit.
A train 240 meters long moving at a speed of 72 km/h crosses a railway platform in 25 seconds. What is the length of the platform?
questions.explanation:
Speed of train in m/s = 72 × (5/18) = 20 m/s.
Total distance covered in 25 seconds = Speed × Time = 20 × 25 = 500 meters.
Total distance = Length of train + Length of platform
500 = 240 + Platform Length
Platform Length = 500 − 240 = 260 meters.

questions.stem: The length and breadth of a rectangular field are in the ratio 5 : 2, and its perimeter is 98 meters. A circular lawn has a radius equal to the breadth of this rectangular field. Find the area of the circular lawn (taking π = 22/7).
questions.explanation:
Perimeter of rectangle = 2(l + b) = 98 ⇒ l + b = 49 m.
Ratio 5 : 2 ⇒ 7x = 49 ⇒ x = 7.
Length = 5 × 7 = 35 m, Breadth = 2 × 7 = 14 m.
Radius of circular lawn r = Breadth = 14 m.
Area of circular lawn = π × r² = (22/7) × 14 × 14 = 616 m².

Statements:
• Only a few laptops are tablets.
• All tablets are computers.

Both conclusions I and II follow

2. Since all tablets are inside computers and no computers is a mobiles, there is no intersection between tablets and mobiles. Hence, Conclusion II follows.
